pages.text: Panteón Rococó: Tiny Desk Concert : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Panteón Rococó: Tiny Desk Concert For over three decades, Panteón Rococó has been at the forefront of Mexican ska. The band's skankin' grooves slide easily between cumbia and Afro-Caribbean rhythms. Panteón Rococó: Tiny Desk Concert October 1, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Michael Zamora/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Panteón Rococó has been at the forefront of Mexican ska for over three decades. With lyrics that stare down its country's toughest sociopolitical struggles, the band's skankin' grooves slide easily between cumbia and Afro-Caribbean rhythms. At El Tiny, the music and the message is heard loud and clear. After "Arreglame el Alma," lead singer Dr. Shenka greets the crowd and launches into "1993…," a devastating testimonial about the countless desaparecidos (missing) throughout Mexico. For the uninitiated, it might seem counterintuitive for such a sensitive subject to be set to upbeat music. But Panteón Rococó's frenetic energy allows for an emotional and physical release of the despair and hopelessness of daily life that can beset modern Mexico. And when surrounded by others hopping up and down, singing songs of resistance, you're no longer alone. pages.text: Paradata Paradata Skip Navigation Paradata About Working Papers About About Working Papers About What is paradata? Paradata is a term used to describe data generated as a by-product of the data collection process. Types of paradata vary from contact attempt history records for interviewer-assisted operations, to form tracing using tracking numbers in mail surveys, to keystroke or mouse-click history for internet self-response surveys. Because paradata are a by-product of a given data collection operation, the format, layout and content of paradata are a function of the system that generated the data. Integrating these data requires a variety of software and statistical tools. These challenges are worth overcoming, however, as paradata can be informative about the progress, cost and quality of both particular data collection operations and overall survey management. Why does the Census Bureau need paradata? Nonresponse in federal surveys increasing as budgets for data collection are decreasing. In order to gather and provide accurate information on the U.S. population and economy in a cost-effective manner, we need to utilize our resources efficiently. Paradata can help us identify potential areas of improvement, implement changes, and then evaluate the effect of those changes. Paradata are used for a variety of reasons across the Bureau, in order to: Measure and limit contact burden in our federal surveys. Time reminder mailings and contacts based on outgoing and incoming mail tracking. Selectively assign data collection features, such as incentives, shorter questionnaires

Photograph: Louis Grasse/PX/Zuma/Shutterstock US television industry This article is more than 1 year old Paramount pays $7.7bn for exclusive US rights deal with UFC This article is more than 1 year old Deal ends sport’s pay-per-view model and comes days after Hollywood studio’s merger with Skydance Media Mark Sweney Mon 11 Aug 2025 11.08 EDT Last modified on Tue 12 Aug 2025 08.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Paramount has struck a $7.7bn (£5.7bn) deal to become the exclusive US broadcaster of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, just days after its controversial merger with Skydance Media. Under the seven-year deal with the sports group’s parent company, TKO Group, all 13 of UFC’s marquee numbered events and 30 Fight Nights a year will be streamed on the Paramount+ service, with a selected number also simulcast on CBS, from next year. The agreement will mean the end of UFC’s current pay-per-view model on the Disney-owned ESPN+ service. The deal comes a week after David Ellison took over as chair and chief executive following Skydance’s $8.4bn takeover of the Hollywood studio and broadcasting business, with the media company saying it may pursue UFC rights in other markets as they come up for renewal

Parents: Help Children Fight Flu Sept. 17, 2024 What to know Influenza (flu) is a contagious respiratory disease caused by influenza viruses. Flu can be more dangerous than the common cold for children. Each year, flu places a large burden on the health and well-being of children and their families. Annual flu vaccination offers the best protection against flu and its potentially serious complications in children. Parents can help children fight flu by getting themselves and their children vaccinated against flu each year. Overview Children younger than 5 years old—especially those younger than 2—and children of any age with certain chronic health conditions, like asthma and diabetes, are at higher risk of developing potentially serious flu complications. Because these groups of children are at higher risk, it is especially important that they get a seasonal flu vaccine to help prevent flu, and to reduce their risk of being hospitalized or dying from flu if they do get sick. Size comparisons for PM particles PM stands for particulate matter (also called particle pollution): the term for a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets found in the air. Some particles, such as dust, dirt, soot, or smoke, are large or dark enough to be seen with the naked eye. Others are so small they can only be detected using an electron microscope. Particle pollution includes: PM 10 : inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 10 micrometers and smaller; and PM 2.5 : fine inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 2.5 micrometers and smaller. How small is 2.5 micrometers? Think about a single hair from your head. The average human hair is about 70 micrometers in diameter – making it 30 times larger than the largest fine particle. In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility. But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong. "I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense." Figure caption, Complete and utter nonsense - Cummins Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. pages.text: Peace Corps Volunteers | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Peace Corps Volunteers Federal Employees’ Compensation Program A Peace Corps Volunteer who sustains an injury or illness in performance of their Peace Corps service may be entitled to benefits under the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA). The FECA, administered by the Department's Office of Workers' Compensation Programs (OWCP), provides medical, wage loss and other compensation benefits for Peace Corps Volunteers who sustain injury or illness while in the performance of duty. Peace Corps Volunteers are considered to be in the performance of duty while abroad during the period of Peace Corps service for purposes of FECA coverage. An injury sustained outside the United States is deemed proximately caused by such service, unless the injury or illness was caused by willful misconduct, intention to bring about injury or death, or intoxication. FECA benefits may also be provided for an injury or illness present prior to entering Peace Corps service, if evidence supports that Peace Corps service contributed to a worsening of the condition. The Peace Corps provides medical and dental care that covers all related expenses during service, including preventative care and issues incurred during training period. Until you are separated from the Peace Corps, you are encouraged to seek medical and dental care from the Peace Corps . Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Pechuck Lookout In the early 20th century, a growing concern for fire protection in forested areas resulted in the construction of lookouts with wide views throughout the Pacific Northwest. Located on the Table Rock Trail, within the BLM Northwest Oregon District boundary, the Pechuck Lookout was established in 1918, at an elevation of 4,338 feet. Originally, the lookout consisted only of a primitive fire detection rangefinder; and some years later, in the early 1930s, a small stone and wood cabin was built. The Pechuck Lookout, also known as a cupola, was built by John Oblack, a Czechoslovakian from Molalla with help from an unknown stone mason from Portland. The cupola-type lookout was built primarily with native stone from sources nearby and the lower story served as the living quarters for hearty individuals staffing the fire lookout. The upper story has windows on all four sides and provides a 360-degree view of the surrounding landscape. Until 1932, the only access to the lookout site was by way of the Table Rock Trail through what is now Table Rock Wilderness. Identificação em campo de Handroanthus impetiginosus (Ipê-roxo-de-bola) 📚 Sou pesquisador da área ambiental então sempre tento mostrar o potencial que o mapeamento para o OpenStreetMap possui. Os resultados abaixo são relacionados às árvores mapeadas e identificadas no local do parque, um trabalho que iniciei faz mais de seis meses e está quase 100% pronto. Quem quiser acompanhar esses e outros mapeamentos, costumo divulgá-los no Instagram - OMapaPB . 🗺️ Esses mapas mostram as espécies de árvores que existem no parque atualmente. A identificação foi feita por chaves botânicas disponíveis na Plataforma Reflora e SiBBr, literatura da Embrapa e, principalmente, a coleção de livros sobre espécies arbóreas brasileiras e exóticas de Lorenzi. 🌲 As principais árvores encontradas são de espécies exóticas como as mungubas, algarobeiras, flamboyants e os ipês-rosa-de-el-salvador que é muitas vezes plantado como nativo por várias prefeituras. People at Increased Risk for Food Poisoning Jan. 31, 2025 Key points Certain groups of people are at higher risk for severe illness from foodborne illness. Higher risk groups include people who are 65 and older, children under 5, people with weakened immune systems, and pregnant women. People at increased risk Anyone can get food poisoning, but certain groups of people are more likely to get very sick from food poisoning. For these people, their body may not be able to fight germs and sickness as effectively. It's especially important to take steps to prevent food poisoning if you or someone you care for belong to one of the groups below. People 65 and older People aged 65 and older are at increased risk for food poisoning. As people age, their immune systems and organs don't recognize and get rid of harmful germs as well as they once did. This increases the chance they'll get sick from food poisoning. Nearly half of people aged 65 and older who have a lab-confirmed foodborne illness from Salmonella , Campylobacter , Listeria or E. coli are hospitalized. January 30, 2025 People at Increased Risk for Illness from Animals What to know Anyone can get sick from germs animals can carry, but some people are more likely to get sick and have more serious illness. Riskier animals include rodents, reptiles, amphibians, and poultry. These people don't need to avoid all contact with animals but should be aware of the risks and take steps to protect themselves. High-risk animals Turtles can carry germs that can make some people very sick. These animals are more likely to carry germs that can make people sick: Reptiles and amphibians (lizards, snakes, turtles, frogs) Backyard poultry (chickens, ducks, turkeys, geese) Rodents (hamsters, guinea pigs, rats, mice, and other small rodents) Exotic pets (monkeys and other wild animals) Even animals that look clean and healthy can carry harmful germs, and areas where animals live or roam can be contaminated – you don’t have to touch an animal to get sick. NPS / Tahzay Jones Many parts of Alaska have a hidden underground world of frozen ground. The depth and extent of this “permafrost” varies by location, depending on average air temperatures, soil types, topography, and surface vegetation. Frozen ground is stable, providing a solid foundation for roads and buildings. Permafrost is also impermeable, so water pools on the surface instead of seeping through the soil, and creates a landscape dotted with many small lakes. The shorter and warmer winters are affecting permafrost. – Dave Swanson, Fairbanks Rising temperatures are melting this frozen ground and forever altering the landscape. Without this solid foundation, roads and buildings sink into the softer, non-frozen ground. Sinkholes and slumpages form when their frozen supportive underground layers thaw. And lakes previously formed by permafrost have begun to drain. Melting Permafrost Shifting sands of coastal barrier islands. pages.text: Personal Assistance Services | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Personal Assistance Services More in This Section Close Accessible Technology Communications Access Health Care Housing Personal Assistance Services Transportation Universal Design For many individuals with disabilities, personal assistance services (PAS) help make employment possible. Some people use PAS to carry out activities of daily living. Depending on the individual, such activities might include getting up and ready for work, bathing, dressing, cooking, cleaning, or running errands. Some people also use PAS in the workplace. Examples of workplace PAS vary, but may involve activities such as retrieving materials out of reach or providing travel assistance for an employee with a mobility impairment; helping an employee with a cognitive disability in decision-making; reading printed materials to an employee who is visually impaired; or ensuring a sign language interpreter is present during meetings for an employee who is deaf. Whether at home or work, PAS can be essential to employment success. Recognizing this, ODEP works to expand and raise awareness of employment-related PAS options. Meeting the needs of people on and off the job raises important policy issues for federal and state governments, service providers, and employers, as well as people with disabilities themselves. History In 2010, a paper map by 3dShapes was digitized and imported, to map landuse in Nederland. The import project was well conducted and properly documented in the OSM-wiki. This was a major step in filling in the space on OSM. Some problems remained after import, to be dealt with later. For instance, where trees had been planted in multiple rows, it was imported as an orchard. As a result, our motorways were suddenly lined with orchards, on OSM-based maps. This has been fixed by organized mappings. Another example: the paper map had a tile grid of thin black lines. These lines were seen as cut lines, resulting in unnecessary and awkward splits of the imported areas. The import procedure did detect this problem, but couldn’t automate a fix, so this was left to the future mappers. It took 15 years before a crazy mapper got rid of this in a solo project lasting 2 months. Guess who? The issue Not much of a problem, more of an annoyance, really: All polygons were tagged with “source=3dShapes”. A significant part of the polygons still carry this source tag. pages.text: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81 - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Peter Storey won 19 caps for England Published 17 November 2026 Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals. He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee. "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement. "All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. "We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund." Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield. He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions. Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72. He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired. Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble? 23 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Liv McMahon , Technology reporter and Osmond Chia , Business reporter How did AI discover the internet's massive cyber-security risk? For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks. Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout , urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline. There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far. But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world. What is PHP? Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily. It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server. Located approximately 100 miles (161 km) northeast of Fairbanks, this 27-mile (44 km) hiking trail traverses a series of alpine ridge tops entirely above timberline. The trail was built for hikers, but is open to all forms of non-motorized use. The Pinnell Mountain Trail is marked with rock cairns as it crosses open tundra with views north to the Yukon River and south to the Alaska Range. Wooden posts along the trail show the mileage from the start at Eagle Summit to the trail's end at Twelvemile Summit.
